name: Antelopus Selan Energy Ltd
title: Antelopus Selan Energy Ltd-$ - 530075 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Onshore E&P ramping: October output ~2,000 BOEPD against a 2,500 exit guide for FY27, with Q2 volumes flat QoQ, realisations down 7% and EBITDA margin ~71% at ~$88 oil.

capex.quote: Then we went to Rs.160 crores. Again, we went to Rs.87 crores, then Rs.220 crores, hopefully Rs.250 crores this year.

summary.headline: Q2 FY27 EBITDA rose to Rs.90 crore (about 71% margin, Rs.83 crore or 69% ex one-off) on flat volumes; exit guidance 2,500 BOEPD, 5,000 BOPD by FY29.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of Rs.121.7 crore and net profit of Rs.57.3 crore, with volumes flat QoQ and realised oil down to $88.2/bbl from $95.3/bbl. Management reiterated a 2,500 BOEPD exit for FY27 and 3,500 BOEPD next year, with 5,000 BOPD targeted by FY29 on onshore assets only. The company signed two KG Onshore and Cambay Basin revenue sharing contracts (DSF IV) on 22 October 2026. Bakrol's 10-well campaign is complete, Karjisan's seven-well campaign is under way, and October production was about 2,000 BOEPD. Balance sheet is debt-free with about Rs.100 crore cash and liquid investments and Rs.780 crore equity.

segments.name: Cambay Basin (Bakrol, Karjisan, Lohar, Cambay)
segments.commentary: Bakrol average about 950 BOE/d in October after the 10-well drilling and fracking campaign; Karjisan (PSC, royalty and cess under 5% of top line) has seven wells planned this fiscal, two drilled but not yet on production. Cambay field (50% JV with Synergia) has one to two optionality wells planned for late Feb/early Mar 2027.

segments.name: KG Onshore
segments.commentary: Seven new discoveries added, about nine fields in total, of which only Mukkamala is producing; management says resource base may be larger than the offshore portfolio. Single-rig, multi-well appraisal planned; a resource estimate to follow after third-party reserve work. Wells expected to cost about $10 million more than Cambay's roughly $1.5 million.

segments.name: Duarmara (Assam, JV)
segments.commentary: Duarmara-4Z found oil in the TIPAM-1 zone rather than the expected gas; oil recirculated to surface twice. Well cost about Rs.60-70 crore, and a plan covering wells 1, 2 and 4 is due over the next five to six months. Gas monetisation is constrained by Assam's lack of National Grid connection.

segments.name: Offshore
segments.commentary: Treated as optionality; excluded from the 5,000 BOPD guidance, with management focus shifting to it in FY28-29.

guidance_outlook: Exit FY27 at about 2,500 BOEPD, with Karjisan's seven wells and the Cambay optionality wells as the main drivers; October production was about 2,000 BOEPD (one answer cited about 1,950).
Exit FY28 at about 3,500 BOEPD and FY29 at about 5,000 BOEPD, onshore only; minimal contribution assumed from KG and Duarmara.
EBITDA margin expected to stay above 65% for the year; management says its endeavour is to keep margins in line.
Capex guided at Rs.250 crore for FY27 (against Rs.220 crore in FY26), with funding via internal accruals for now; no commitment on debt or equity raises.
KG Onshore development plan and capex guidance to come after field development plans are filed with regulators; Duarmara oil plan in five to six months.
capex_capacity: Bakrol 10-well campaign complete (drilling and fracking); production response showing Bakrol as a multi-year growth field.
Karjisan: seven wells planned for FY27; two drilled, first perforation expected within about a week, rig back on site.
Cambay field: one to two optionality wells planned for late Feb/early Mar 2027; field area about 160 sq km.
Duarmara: well cost Rs.60-70 crore; TIPAM-1 oil zone; partner alignment needed.
Historical capex: Rs.51 crore (FY23), Rs.160 crore (FY24), Rs.87 crore (FY25), Rs.220 crore (FY26), Rs.250 crore (FY27 target).
demand_pricing: Pricing is linked to international crude benchmarks; Cambay crude sells at about a 10% discount to dated Brent on average, with most volumes to Indian Oil and about 20% to private buyers at a slightly higher discount.
Realised oil ran about $76 in July, $84 in August and above $100 in September.
Royalty and cess are about 30% of top line in Bakrol and Cambay versus under 5% in Karjisan, averaging about 15-16% of revenue.
Variable handling cost is about $1-1.5 per barrel on ONGC tolling; fixed costs are about 70-75% of the cost base.
Management's investment hurdle: double-digit returns at $65-70/bbl, cash back within one to one-and-a-half years, and no loss at $50/bbl.
Assam gas is sold at a discount to APM prices because Assam is not connected to the National Grid; oil is easier to truck out.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins above 65% be sustained for the full year as costs stay flat while volumes grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fixed costs are 70-75% of the cost base and incremental barrels are cheaper in Cambay; KG will add establishment costs, but margins should hold. Management's stated aim is to keep margins in line, not a firm guarantee.

qa_highlights.question: How much incremental revenue will Karjisan and Bakrol add, and does the 2,500 exit depend on Cambay?
qa_highlights.answer: Bakrol is at about 950 BOE/d. Karjisan's seven wells are already in the 2,500 exit figure, which management said has no ambiguity; Cambay optionality wells sit outside it and could take production beyond 5,000.

qa_highlights.question: How will KG Onshore be funded and ramped up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to decide between internal accruals, debt or equity; it will start with one rig, drill a couple of wells and then decide on a bigger campaign. Wells cost about $10 million more than Cambay wells.

qa_highlights.question: What pricing formula and price range should be used for sensitivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing is set by a crude-yield-based discount to dated Brent (about 10%), and investments are screened at $50-70/bbl. Management gave no explicit bear-to-bull range.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Duarmara oil potential, capex per well and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Well cost Rs.60-70 crore with 3.5 km wells. Oil is light, and flow and frac options are being studied. A concrete estimate is expected next fiscal, not this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is CWIP high and why are deferred tax liabilities rising?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs.100 crore of the Rs.190 crore CWIP is Duarmara, to be capitalised on production. Deferred tax is rising because drilling capex is fully expensed for tax; it may partly reverse if drilling slows.

risks_watch: Duarmara gas evacuation and oil development path are unresolved, with the TIPAM-1 oil zone yet to be tested and the JV partner to be aligned.
KG Onshore high-pressure, high-temperature wells cost about $10 million more each; no resource or reserve estimate yet.
Karjisan's seven wells and the Cambay optionality wells (with Synergia) need to deliver to reach 2,500 BOEPD exit and 5,000 BOPD by FY29.
Realisations are sensitive to crude; September's above-$100 prices lifted the average, and private buyers' purchasing has been limited at higher prices.
Growing deferred tax liability and the chance of a funding decision (debt or equity) once KG ramps up.
Management's first investor call; one-off Rs.6.5 crore refund included in other income.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-leaning on the Cambay ramp-up, with a clear 2,500 BOEPD exit and 5,000 BOPD FY29 target. Cautious and deliberately vague on KG Onshore, Duarmara and offshore, explicitly declining to give capex, reserve or funding numbers beyond the onshore guidance.
key_quotes: So, at $65-$70, if a project gives me double-digit return and gets me back my cash within year to year and a half, that is a go project for me.
Karjisan has the best fiscals in our portfolio as of today, because it has concessional Cess and royalty rates to it, because it is still in its primary term as a production-sharing contract.
So, the 5000 barrel plant that you have has a very subdued KG or the Cambay optionality in it.
Oil does not need pipeline infrastructure. Oil I can just put into a truck to haul across 300 kilometers and sell to refiner somewhere, right?

growth.why: Management reiterates an FY27 exit of about 2,500 BOEPD (October run-rate about 2,000 BOEPD) and 5,000 BOPD by FY29 onshore, backed by Karjisan's seven wells (two drilled, rig back on site), Cambay optionality wells and FY27 capex of Rs.250 crore; Q2 volumes were flat QoQ and the exit ramp depends on wells not yet on production.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides EBITDA margin above 65% for FY27 (Q2 at 71%, or 69% ex Rs.6.5 crore one-off), with fixed costs at 70-75% of the cost base and incremental Cambay barrels cheaper, though it is an aim, not a firm guarantee and KG will add establishment costs.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Exit FY27 at about 2,500 BOEPD from October run-rate of about 2,000 BOEPD, driven by Karjisan's seven wells (two drilled, first perforation within about a week) and Cambay optionality wells planned for late Feb/early Mar 2027; the 2,500 exit already includes Karjisan but not Cambay optionality.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Volumes rose from about 1,700 BOEPD H1 average toward the 2,000 BOEPD October run-rate and a 2,500 BOEPD FY27 exit, but Q2 volumes were flat QoQ and the ramp depends on wells not yet producing.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex is already guided at Rs.250 crore (up from Rs.220 crore), and KG Onshore development capex and a Duarmara oil plan (Rs.60-70 crore per well) will follow in five to six months or after field development plans are filed, but no figures are committed yet.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was held (2,500 BOEPD FY27 exit, 5,000 BOPD FY29), and October production of about 2,000 BOEPD plus Bakrol's 950 BOE/d and Karjisan's wells leave room, but realisations fell to $88.2/bbl from $95.3/bbl and September's above-$100 price lifted the average.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Exit and FY29 targets depend on Karjisan wells and Cambay optionality wells being delivered, and realisations are crude-sensitive (July about $76, August $84, September above $100), with private buyers limiting purchases at higher prices.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: KG Onshore (seven new discoveries, about nine fields, only Mukkamala producing) and Duarmara oil (TIPAM-1 zone) could add new production, but KG resource estimates and Duarmara plans are not due for several months and minimal KG/Duarmara contribution is assumed for FY28-29.

rows.label: Two KG Onshore and Cambay DSF IV revenue sharing contracts signed
rows.why: Two revenue sharing contracts (KG Onshore and Cambay Basin, DSF IV) were signed on 22 October 2026, adding acreage that supports the onshore growth story.

rows.label: Debt-free balance sheet with cash buffer for capex
rows.why: No borrowings and about Rs.100 crore cash and liquid investments against Rs.250 crore FY27 capex funded from internal accruals for now, though a debt or equity decision is possible once KG ramps up.

rows.label: Assam gas monetisation constrained by no National Grid link
rows.why: Assam gas sells at a discount to APM prices because Assam is not connected to the National Grid, so Duarmara's gas contribution is unlikely to add near-term revenue.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Cambay and Karjisan ramp to a 2,500 BOEPD exit and held FY29 5,000 BOPD, but was cautious and vague on KG Onshore, Duarmara and offshore funding and capex; analysts pressed on margin sustainability, KG funding, and the crude sensitivity of realisations.
